summary: EU values and transparency commissioner Vera Jourova warned on 26 Sept 2023 that generative AI and deepfakes threaten elections, notably the European Parliament vote next year, and urged signatories of the voluntary Code of Practice on Disinformation to strengthen safeguards. A second batch of signatory reports (January to June) was published, with Google, Meta, Microsoft and TikTok describing their AI measures. Jourova also stressed countering Kremlin propaganda, fact-checking and data access for researchers, and criticized X/Twitter, which left the Code in May.
one_line: EU commissioner Vera Jourova urges platforms to boost generative AI and deepfake safeguards ahead of 2024 EU elections, as new Code of Practice on Disinformation reports are published.
key_facts: Vera Jourova, the EU's values and transparency commissioner, said on 26 Sept 2023 that the risks of AI-generated disinformation are "particularly high in the context of elections" ahead of the pan-EU vote for a new European Parliament next year.
Jourova was due to meet OpenAI, maker of ChatGPT, the same day; OpenAI is not a signatory to the EU's Code of Practice on Disinformation.

This summer Jourova urged Code signatories to label deepfakes and AI-generated content and to create a dedicated, separate track to tackle "AI production", quipping that machines should not have free speech.

The EU AI Act is expected to make user disclosures a legal requirement for makers of generative AI, but it is still draft legislation and is not expected to apply for a couple of years, so the Commission is using the Code as a stop-gap.

The Digital Services Act (DSA) obliges very-large-online-platforms (VLOPs) and search engines to assess and mitigate societal risks such as disinformation, with fines up to 6% of global annual turnover.

The Code has 44 signatories, including platforms, the ad industry and fact-checking civil society groups; a second batch of reports covering January to June was published, with reports from Google, Meta, Microsoft and TikTok among the first available.

Google plans to use the IPTC Photo Metadata Standard to add metadata tags to images generated by Google AI, so Search can display an AI-generated label, and has no additional YouTube measures planned for the next six months.

Microsoft cited its Responsible AI standard v.2, Project Providence with Truepic, and partnerships with C2PA, EFE Verifica and Reporters Sans Frontières, but committed to no specific new Bing steps over the next six months.

TikTok requires users to proactively disclose AI-generated or manipulated content showing realistic scenes, and is a launch partner of the Partnership on AI's Responsible Practices for Synthetic Media.
Meta is launching a Community Forum on Generative AI with Stanford Deliberative Democracy Lab and the Behavioural Insights Team, and will join the Code's working group on AI-generated disinformation.

YouTube shut down more than 400 channels between January and April 2023 tied to the Russian-state-sponsored Internet Research Agency and removed ads from almost 300 sites linked to state-funded propaganda.
TikTok fact-checked 832 war-related videos, of which 211 were removed; Bing promoted or downgraded information for almost 800,000 Ukraine-related queries.
Elon Musk took Twitter (now X) out of the Code in May; X was designated a VLOP under the DSA in April, and early analysis found it performed worst for disinformation ratios.
